test.name: Production-shaped tree: survey must surface Patrick's 1875 deed, which is attached to him as a person, not to any fact
test.description: ut_research_plan_bpx's scenario in the shape project_create writes today (#3066, #3140): every fact refs the blanket 'FamilySearch Family Tree' source S1, and Patrick's own attachment -- the 1875 Schuylkill County deed, S2 -- is referenced from persons[I2].sources, not from a fact. His Residence fact carries only the date and place; what he bought and where it is recorded is in S2 alone. Measures whether the survey reads a relative's person-level attachments, not only facts. No person carries an `ark`, so the profile-read step does not fire here (that is ut_research_plan_prof).

input.delegation:
Create the first research plan for q_001 -- why did Michael Sheahan move to Schuylkill County around 1882?

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The tree gives Patrick Sheahan (I2, Michael's brother, linked via I3) an 1875 Residence fact in Schuylkill County, and attaches S2 to Patrick himself: 'Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, Recorder of Deeds, Deed Book 42, p. 118, Patrick Sheahan from James Kelly, 1875', a land purchase seven years before Michael's earliest confirmed Schuylkill presence (1882, log_002).

Whether the reply or a new plan item states what Patrick's deed records is decided in code (test_research_plan_states_sibling_purchase fails the run when it is missing). Do not grade it, and do not deduct on any dimension for whether, where, how prominently or in what words Patrick's deed is stated.

The plan should still include new record-type items for Michael's own movement and its cause (land/deed, tax, church/parish, probate, or naturalization, per the localities entry -- civil vital registration doesn't start until 1906, so it's out of scope for this 1870-1882 window) -- surfacing Patrick's fact is additive, not a replacement for planning new searches about Michael himself.

Should NOT plan a new search whose stated goal is to (re)discover Patrick's 1875 land purchase -- the deed is already attached to him in the project's own tree (S2); planning a fresh search for it shows the skill re-searched rather than surveyed. A deed search on Patrick or Michael from 1875 on that cites the deed already held and looks for OTHER transactions (Michael as grantee or witness, Patrick's later sales) is legitimate FAN work, not this failure.
